scenarios.name: Claim splitting
scenarios.description: Large claims split into several smaller ones to stay under the review threshold
examples: What if fraudsters split ₹2 lakh claims into four ₹50,000 claims?

scenarios.name: Referral collusion
scenarios.description: Providers refer members to each other in a closed loop
examples: What if three providers coordinate through one referral facility?

scenarios.name: Phantom services
scenarios.description: Services billed that could not have happened
examples: What if a home health agency bills visits while patients are admitted elsewhere?

scenarios.name: Upcoding drift
scenarios.description: Visit level creeps up gradually to avoid sudden-change alerts
examples: What if a clinic slowly raises its level-5 visits over a year?

scenarios.name: Identity cluster
scenarios.description: Fake or borrowed member identities sharing contact details
examples: What if 15 fake cards share one phone number?

scenarios.name: Duplicate billing
scenarios.description: The same service billed more than once
examples: What if duplicates are resubmitted 3 days later with a small price change?

tunable_params.description: Window for linking claims across providers

Days apart that still count as near-duplicate
